Attention, pantry pilgrims: The kettles beat like war drums and the air smells of rosemary and thunder. Doors rattle; shelves murmur; sacks of grain lean to listen. In the hush between ladle and flame, an oath is spoken that tastes like smoke and salt. And from that oath rises the Bean Supreme. They were not crowned in marble halls, but in a village kitchen the night the hearth-guilds failed and winter clawed at every sill. An apprentice cook-witch stirred the Common Pot until the broth sang, traced sigils in steam, and invoked the ancient Legume Rite—Soak, Stir, Share. The beans awoke, each a bright little heartbeat, and the pot swelled with courage; from its brim stepped a figure in a can-crown, bearing the Master Spoon as scepter. Sprouts bent like pennons in a gale; the first oaths were sworn over bread and brine, and the pantry—once a quiet room of keeping—became a chapel of uprising. Word raced along roads and root-cellars alike: hoarded larders were broken, lonely fires rekindled, and the meek were provisioned in the Overlord’s name. The war that followed was brief and boiling. Against the Salt Barons and their iron cauldrons marched millers, picklers, and fieldhands beneath stew-stitched banners; Bigger Beans rolled like sling-stones; the Bean Collective hummed one stout harmony that made sieges feel like supper. By ladle-law the Overlord decreed: No grief in the garden. No false weights at market. No dupe of bread or bean. Consent in spice, kindness in word, and every pot with an off-switch. When the final lid clattered, a Commons Pot was raised at the crossroads—ever-warm, ever-watchful—so travelers might ladle hope without cost. And should famine or foolishness return, the rite endures: strike the Master Spoon thrice on the can-crown, whisper share the beans, and the Overlord will answer—quiet as a simmer, unstoppable as a boil.

It also works outside of claims entirely, protecting your stuff on unclaimed land too.

Make your own shop, fill it, and help people find it.
Want to see one first? Run  in-game.

You need 3 things: A claim. Your shop must be inside your own claim, or a friend's claim if they  you. See the Claims Guide.A barrel. Only barrels can be shops. Chests don't work.The items you want to sell.

Put down a barrel. Keep the block in front of it empty. The shop sign goes there.Hold the item you want to sell. How many you hold is how many people get each time they buy. Hold 1 diamond, and people buy 1 diamond. Hold 64 dirt, and people buy 64 dirt.Sneak (hold Shift) and left-click the barrel.Chat asks for a price. Type only a number, like , and press Enter. A sign appears on the barrel. Your shop is made! There is no "shop made" message. The sign is how you know.
Right-click the barrel to open it.Put your items inside.The sign now says Selling and a number. The number is how many times people can buy, not how many items.

Left-click the sign to buy once. It buys right away. There is no "are you sure?".Want more? Sneak + left-click the sign. Then type how many, or . Tip: Don't punch your own shop sign. You buy from yourself and your chat fills up.

Right-click your shop's sign. A menu opens in chat. Press T to open chat, then click a button: Price [Change]: type the new price.Items per trade [Change]: how many items people get each time they buy. Set the price again after this. It doesn't change by itself![Switch to buying] or [Switch to selling]: change what your shop does.[Remove Shop]: click it, then click it again within 5 seconds. Commands work too, while you look at your shop: sets the price to 5 sells 16 items each time removes the shop. Your items stay in the barrel.

A buying shop pays people for their items. Make a shop like normal.Right-click the sign and click [Switch to buying]. The sign now says Buying.Keep money in your balance. That's what pays people.Keep empty space in the barrel. People left-click the sign to sell you their items.
